note: First-pass coverage map. Objective titles are paraphrased; confirm wording and sub-bullets against the official CompTIA objectives PDFs. Statuses were set from notes section titles and item counts, not a full read, so review each one. Run: npm run report:objectives

objectives.title: Monitor mobile-device hardware and use appropriate replacement techniques
objectives.note: Notes teach model-specific inspection, monitoring and replacement planning for batteries, RAM/storage, keyboard/input, wireless parts and displays; the lab uses manufacturer service guidance and post-service verification.

objectives.title: Compare and contrast accessories and connectivity options for mobile devices
objectives.note: Notes compare wired/wireless connection methods, tethering, NFC/RFID roles, docks, port replicators and mobile accessories with compatibility boundaries.

objectives.title: Configure basic mobile-device network connectivity and application support
objectives.note: Basic Wi-Fi/cellular/Bluetooth, hotspot, application permissions and managed-device checks are taught. SIM/eSIM provisioning, location/synchronization and the complete objective scope need additional teaching.

objectives.title: Compare and contrast TCP and UDP ports, protocols, and their purposes
Explain wireless networking technologies
objectives.note: Notes compare 802.11 generations, bands, widths, channels/regulatory limits, Bluetooth, NFC and RFID. Cards and scenario questions reinforce client/AP compatibility and throughput limits.

objectives.title: Summarize services provided by networked hosts
objectives.note: DNS, DHCP, storage, proxy, UTM, spam gateway, load balancer, NTP, syslog and AAA covered; mail servers and legacy/embedded systems still thin.

objectives.title: Explain common network configuration concepts
objectives.note: DNS records, DHCP terms (scope, range, exclusion, reservation, lease, options), VLANs and VPNs (concentrator, client-to-site, site-to-site, always-on, clients) taught in networking-dns-dhcp, with questions, cards, a PBQ and drill items.

objectives.title: Compare and contrast common networking hardware
Configure a basic wired or wireless SOHO network
objectives.note: Mapped notes teach IPv4/IPv6, private/public/link-local addressing, static/dynamic settings, masks/prefixes and gateways. The new SOHO notes and paper lab add router/AP setup, DHCP, DNS, WLAN selection and ordered verification; no live configuration is required.

objectives.title: Compare and contrast internet connection types and network types
objectives.note: The new notes compare fiber, cable, DSL, satellite, cellular and fixed wireless service and define PAN, LAN, WLAN, MAN, WAN and SAN with explicit scope distinctions.

objectives.title: Explain networking tools and their purposes
Compare and contrast display components and attributes
objectives.note: The notes introduce every explicitly listed display type, touch/digitizer, inverter, and attribute, but do not yet teach enough comparative tradeoffs among TN, IPS, and VA panel modes to support the objective’s compare-and-contrast task. Brightness and contrast ratio are useful supplemental context, not separately enumerated attributes in v4.0.

objectives.title: Summarize cable types, connectors, and their purposes
Compare and contrast RAM characteristics
objectives.note: The new notes distinguish SO-DIMM/DIMM, DDR generation/keying, ECC and channel-population compatibility, but do not yet give a sufficiently complete comparison of the listed RAM characteristics across supported platforms.

objectives.title: Compare and contrast storage devices
Install and configure motherboards, CPUs, and add-on cards
Install the appropriate power supply
Deploy and configure multifunction devices and printers
objectives.note: Printer types covered; drivers, sharing, and configuration not found.

objectives.title: Perform appropriate printer maintenance
objectives.note: Maintenance by printer type taught in core1-printers, plus step-level detail (maintenance kit and page counter, toner handling, calibration, cleaning, inkjet heads, thermal element, impact ribbon and printhead), with questions, cards, a PBQ and the Printer Drill.

objectives.title: Explain virtualization concepts
Summarize cloud-computing concepts
Troubleshoot motherboards, RAM, CPUs, and power
objectives.note: Symptom tables for power, POST, boot order, stop errors, black screen after Windows loads, heat, burning smell, capacitors, noises and sluggish performance in core1-ch1-motherboards, with questions, cards, a PBQ and drill items.

objectives.title: Troubleshoot drives and RAID arrays
objectives.note: Drive and RAID symptom tables (click of death, read/write errors, S.M.A.R.T., read-only SSD, boot device and OS not found, uninitialized drives, power, mapped drives, IOPS, RAID failure per level, inactive volumes) in core1-ch2, with questions, cards, a PBQ and drill items.

objectives.title: Troubleshoot video, projector, and display issues
Troubleshoot common mobile-device issues
Troubleshoot network issues
objectives.note: Network symptom table (link light, port flapping, intermittent wireless and interference, APIPA, gateway, DNS, slow speeds, latency, jitter and VoIP, authentication failures, time-of-day problems) in core1-ch9-wireless-soho, alongside the tools in networking-cabling and quick-reference, with questions, cards, a PBQ and drill items.

objectives.title: Troubleshoot printer issues
